Notes: Turner 6333 divasá 'day' gives European Romani dives and Paluli dīs; the separate source Zargari dis 'day' is already linked to 6333. The grammar explicitly prints dis-este 'every day' as a locative expression of 'every' (p. 132 §3.1.16) and lists diseste in its temporal adverbs (p. 143 §3.20.1.2). The local ending is retained; the inherited day stem is the etymological target. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change. Turner 10702 rā́trī 'night' gives European Romani rat and locative rati 'at night'. The grammar explicitly prints rājt-ādu 'every night' as another locative expression of 'every' (p. 132 §3.1.16), lists rājtādu among temporal adverbs, and separately prints rāt 'night' in the phrase nāklās rāt 'last night' (p. 143 §3.20.1.2). The source j glide and the locative ending are retained; no separately installed bare-night lemma is assumed.
